messages:
Alex: Heads-up — running spike on KV prefetch for trace-enrichment. Observed 15-25% p50 latency reduction for small traces when we warm the cache, but ingest size + cost increase ~12%.
Maria: Nice. What's the prefetch trigger? All new traces? or on-demand?
Alex: Prototype prefetches keys when request first seen (on first span), writes to local sidecar with TTL 60s. Prefetch hits ~40% for followups in workflow.
Tomas: 12% ingest cost sounds heavy. Do we charge customers for this? how does billing attribution work?
Jen (SRE): If this increases telemetry envelope size, our cost buckets spike. Need to map to billing keys. Might need per-tenant opt-in.
Alex: Agree — thinking two-tier policy: per-tenant opt-in + global sampling for high-volume tenants. Also tuned eviction: LRU with weighted size + recency.
Maria: How do we measure ROI? p50 drop vs token cost? For traces we care about tail though — p95/p99.
Alex: p95 improved ~8ms in spike, p99 unchanged. So mainly median helps.
Tomas: Could we do lazy prefetch with debounce? Wait 5-10ms for possible coalescing, then prefetch. That buys less waste.
Jen (SRE): What about backpressure? Prefetching could amplify load to kv-store. Need admission control and circuit breaker.
Alex: Yup. Proposed limits: global concurrent prefetches 2000, per-tenant 10 req/s, fallback to async warming via background queue.
TelemetryBot: prefetch-stats digest: prefetch_attempts=124k, hit_rate=39%, avg_kv_latency=4.2ms.
Maria: For rollout plan: canary on dev tenants, flag toggled in console, metric: increase in ingest tokens per tenant and latency change.
Tomas: Also consider eviction by cost weight: items that save >X latency while being small size get high priority. Need a heuristic.
Alex: Draft heuristic: score = saved_ms / log(size_bytes+10). We'll simulate with our trace corpus.
Jen (SRE): One more: ensure tags added for cost attribution: add attribute telemetry.prefetch=true and include billing_key. Otherwise chargeback impossible.
Alex: agreed. Will add 'prefetch=true' and 'prefetch.policy=<policy>' fields. Also keep opt-out header.
Maria: sgtm. Next: who owns implementing admission control? Eng-runtime + Eng-platform?
Tomas: Runtime will implement local sidecar; eng-platform owns global throttles and console toggle.
Alex: I'll open RFC PR with perf numbers and rollout steps.
Maria: thanks — :thumbsup:
